# Project: a terminal phone-book prototype {#sec-ch-project-phonebook} > *"Make it work, make it right, make it fast."* — Kent Beck. ::: {.callout-note} ## What this chapter contains 1. The **problem statement**, written in my own words. 2. A **requirements matrix** that maps every requirement to the chapters of this part that teach the necessary skills. 3. The **design**: classes, data structure (with its cost analysis), persistence, robustness, user experience. 4. A **walkthrough and code review** of the implementation published in the companion repository [`Phone_Book_Python_OOP.ipynb`](https://github.com/matteo-zirilli/ai-projects/blob/main/Phone_Book_Python_OOP.ipynb) ([open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/matteo-zirilli/ai-projects/blob/main/Phone_Book_Python_OOP.ipynb)). 5. A **reference implementation** that applies every refinement suggested by the review, with an executed demonstration and a test suite. 6. **Extensions** to practise further. ::: ## The problem {#sec-project-brief} ::: {.callout-note} ## About this specification This project was the final assignment of the Python course of the master I attended. The specification below is **my own restatement** of the requirements, written for this handbook; it does not reproduce the course material. ::: **Context.** Many developers, system administrators and data people spend their day in a terminal. Opening a graphical application just to look up a phone number interrupts their flow. A small, fast **command-line phone book** fills that gap. Before building a full product, the goal is a **working prototype** that proves the approach is sound and the code is solid. **What the prototype must do.** - **R1 — Interactive console program.** It runs in a terminal (or in a notebook cell) and talks to the user through text prompts. - **R2 — Object-oriented design.** At least two classes: one for a single contact and one for the collection, each with a clear job. - **R3 — Interface separated from logic.** Reading input and printing messages happen outside the classes that model contacts and the phone book. - **R4 — A suitable data structure**, chosen for orderly and efficient storage, with the choice explained. - **R5 — A main menu** with numbered options that a non-expert can use. - **R6 — The basic operations**: add a contact, list all contacts, edit one, delete one, search by first or last name. - **R7 — Persistence in JSON**: contacts are loaded automatically at start-up and saved when the program ends. - **R8 — Robust loading**: a missing, empty or damaged file must not stop the program. - **R9 — Robust input**: wrong values and invalid menu choices are handled with a message, never with a crash. - **R10 — Good terminal experience**: clear messages, a confirmation after each operation, a clean exit that saves the data. - **R11 — Deliverable**: a notebook with commented code that runs from top to bottom, plus a short demonstration of use. **What counts as quality.** Working operations are only half of the job. The other half is a clean architecture: classes with clear responsibilities, coherent methods, readable and commented code. That is what turns a prototype into a base for a real product. ## Requirements matrix {#sec-project-requirements} | # | Requirement | Skills needed | Chapters | |---|---|---|---| | R1 | Interactive console application | `input`/`print`, loops, menus | @sec-ch-variables, @sec-ch-loops | | R2 | OOP: `Contact` and `PhoneBook` classes, separated responsibilities | classes, special methods, encapsulation, composition | @sec-ch-oop | | R3 | Interaction logic outside the domain classes | single responsibility, modules | @sec-solid, @sec-ch-modules | | R4 | Suitable, motivated data structure for ordered, efficient storage | lists, dicts, hashing, sorting, complexity | @sec-ch-collections, @sec-asymptotic | | R5 | Main menu with clear numbered options | conditionals, dispatch tables | @sec-ch-conditionals, @sec-first-class | | R6 | Add, view, edit, delete, search by name/surname | functions, methods, string matching | @sec-ch-functions, @sec-strings | | R7 | JSON persistence, automatic load at start and save at exit | files, JSON, serialisation | @sec-ch-files | | R8 | Missing / empty / corrupted file handled | exceptions, EAFP | @sec-ch-exceptions | | R9 | Invalid input and out-of-menu choices never crash | casting, validation, `try`/`except` | @sec-casting, @sec-try | | R10 | Confirmations, clean exit that saves | UX, `finally`/context managers | @sec-context-managers | | R11 | Notebook: commented code, runnable top to bottom, demo of use | notebooks, docstrings | @sec-dev-environment, @sec-docstrings-functions | : Requirements and where the book teaches them {#tbl-project-requirements} ## Design {#sec-project-design} ### Responsibilities Following R3 (and @sec-solid), the program splits into four responsibilities, each a class (or module, @sec-real-package): ```{mermaid} %%| echo: false %%| fig-cap: "Architecture of the phone book. Arrows are dependencies; the graph is acyclic (@thm-toposort) and the domain does not depend on the interface." flowchart LR UI["ConsoleUI
(menu, input, messages)"] --> BOOK["PhoneBook
(collection, rules)"] UI --> STORE["JsonStorage
(load / save, file format)"] BOOK --> MODEL["Contact
(one record, validation)"] STORE --> MODEL ``` - **`Contact`** — one record; validates its own fields (non-empty name, valid phone number) so that an invalid contact cannot exist (a class invariant, @sec-encapsulation). - **`PhoneBook`** — the collection and its rules: no duplicates, sorted listing, search, edit, delete. No `input`, no `print`. - **`JsonStorage`** — the only component that knows the file format (information hiding, @sec-modularity): loading tolerates a missing, empty or corrupted file; saving is atomic. - **`ConsoleUI`** — the only component that talks to the user. ### The data structure, with its costs What operations dominate? Listing (sorted), adding with a duplicate check, searching by name, editing and deleting. Two candidates: | Operation | `list` of contacts | `dict` keyed by identity `(name, surname, phone)` | |---|---|---| | duplicate check on add | $O(n)$ scan | $O(1)$ expected (@thm-chaining) | | add | $O(1)$ amortised + $O(n)$ check | $O(1)$ expected | | delete a known contact | $O(n)$ (find + shift) | $O(1)$ expected | | search by substring of name | $O(n)$ | $O(n)$ | | sorted listing | $O(n\log n)$ (or $O(n)$ if kept sorted) | $O(n \log n)$ | : Costs of the two candidate structures ($n$ contacts) {#tbl-project-structures} A **dict keyed by an identity tuple** makes the rule "no two identical contacts" cheap and explicit, and Python dicts keep insertion order (@sec-dicts); the sorted view is produced on demand with `sorted` (Timsort, @sec-sorting). Substring search is linear either way (a prefix index or a trie would be needed to do better — irrelevant for a personal phone book with hundreds of entries, where every operation takes microseconds). **Motivation for the notebook**: *"a dict gives $O(1)$ duplicate checks and deletions; at the scale of a personal phone book the difference is negligible, so the decisive reasons are clarity of the uniqueness rule and simplicity of the code."* That is exactly the kind of justification R4 asks for. ### What identifies a contact? Two entries are "the same contact" if they have the same name, surname and phone number, ignoring letter case and spacing in the number. Homonyms with different numbers are allowed (two different "Mario Rossi"). This identity is an **equivalence relation** (@def-equivalence) because it is equality of a key tuple; the sort order is lexicographic on `(surname, name, phone)`, a strict total order on keys (@thm-lex-order). ### Robustness and user experience - Every input goes through a small set of **validated readers** (`ask_text`, `ask_choice`, `ask_yes_no`) that loop until the input is valid (@sec-try) and are **injected** into the UI, so the UI can be tested with scripted input. - Editing and deleting select a contact **from a numbered list of search results**, instead of asking the user to retype the whole contact exactly. - Ctrl+C or end of input (`EOFError`) **save and exit** instead of showing a traceback. - Saving is **atomic** (@sec-atomic-writes): a crash during the save never destroys the phone book. ## Walkthrough of the published implementation {#sec-project-walkthrough} The notebook in `ai-projects` is organised in four cells: the `Contatto` class, the `Rubrica` class, the Google Drive mount, and the main program. The class and method names are in Italian (the menu is generated from them); the notebook includes a glossary. **`Contatto`** stores first name, last name, number and country code (`prefisso`, default 39). Its constructor converts number and country code with `int(...)` and turns a failure into a clear `ValueError`. It defines `__eq__` (all four fields equal) and `__lt__`, which compares the tuples `(cognome, nome)` — so `list.sort()` orders contacts by surname, then name. A helper `input_valid_contact()` reads a contact from the keyboard, looping on `int(input(...))` until the number and country code are numeric. **`Rubrica`** wraps a list (`self._rubrica`), initialised with the `None` sentinel idiom to avoid the mutable-default trap (the code comment explains why). It offers `aggiungi_contatto` (add, refusing exact duplicates via `cerca_contatto`), `visualizza_contatti` (sort, then print), `modifica_contatto` (read the contact to edit, then the replacement, refusing duplicates), `elimina_contatto`, and `ricerca_contatto` (a sub-menu to search by name or by number). Persistence: `load_file_in_rubr` reads the JSON list and rebuilds the contacts; `convert_rubr_dict` turns contacts into dicts using `inspect.signature(Contatto.__init__)` to discover the field names; `load_rubr_in_file` writes the JSON with `indent=4`. **The menu** is built dynamically: `functionlaties()` lists, with `dir(self)`, the public method names that are not in an exclusion list, and the main loop prints them numbered, reads a choice, checks it with `assert`, and calls the method with `getattr(rubr, name)()` — a dispatch table built by introspection (@sec-first-class). The loop ends on `esci` (exit), after which the phone book is saved. **What it does well**: OOP structure with two classes; special methods for equality and ordering; the mutable-default idiom; validation loops on numeric input; handling of `JSONDecodeError`; docstrings on every method; persistence that round-trips; a menu that cannot drift out of sync with the methods. ### Code review: refinements suggested by this book | # | Observation | Why it matters | Suggested change | Chapter | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Phone numbers stored as `int` | leading zeros are lost (`06…` → `6…`); `+`, spaces impossible | store a validated, normalised **string** (E.164) | @sec-casting, @sec-verification | | 2 | `__eq__` defined without `__hash__` | contacts are unhashable: no sets/dict keys, duplicate checks stay $O(n)$ | define `__hash__` on the same key, or use a frozen dataclass | @prp-hash-contract | | 3 | `Rubrica` reads `contatto._nome` etc. | breaks encapsulation of `Contatto` | public read-only attributes or properties | @sec-encapsulation | | 4 | `input_valid_contact` has no `self` and calls `input()` inside the domain class | works only when called on the class; mixes UI and domain (against R3) | move it to the UI layer (or at least `@staticmethod`) | @sec-dataclasses, @sec-solid | | 5 | `cerca_contatto`, `cerca_name` print messages | domain methods with UI side effects; hard to test | return results; let the UI print | @sec-return | | 6 | `assert` used to validate the menu choice | disabled by `python -O` → `IndexError` | an explicit `if` with a message | @sec-assert | | 7 | `os.path.exists` before `open` | LBYL with a race window; an **empty** file raises `JSONDecodeError` and is reported as invalid | EAFP on `FileNotFoundError`; treat empty as an empty book | @exm-toctou | | 8 | Files opened without `encoding=` | accented names may break on another OS | `encoding="utf-8"` | @sec-text-vs-binary | | 9 | Save with mode `"w"` | a crash mid-save truncates the file | atomic write (temp file + `os.replace`) | @sec-atomic-writes | | 10 | Menu built from `dir()` | order is alphabetical, labels derive from method names, renaming a method changes the UI | an explicit dispatch table (label → function) | @sec-first-class | | 11 | Edit/delete require retyping the whole contact | error-prone UX; the notebook's own to-do notes the "name exists but number differs" case | pick from a numbered list of search results | @sec-project-design | | 12 | `Ctrl+C` / end of input | a traceback, and unsaved data | catch `KeyboardInterrupt`/`EOFError`, save, exit | @sec-try | | 13 | Data structure choice not motivated in the notebook | R4 asks for it explicitly | a text cell with the analysis of @tbl-project-structures | @sec-choosing-collection | | 14 | No automated tests | regressions go unnoticed | a small test suite with scripted input | @sec-verification | : Code review of the published implementation {#tbl-project-review} None of these prevents the prototype from working — it passed the course assessment. They are the difference between a prototype and a product, which is exactly the next step a real product would need. ## Reference implementation {#sec-project-reference} The code below applies all the refinements. It is written as four blocks that correspond to the four modules of @sec-real-package (`models`, `book`, `storage`, `cli`); in a notebook each block is one cell, in a package one file. ### `models`: the contact {.deep} ::: {#5e31bd56 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} """models — the Contact record and its validation.""" from __future__ import annotations import re from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict _SEPARATORS = " -.()" def normalize_phone(text: str, default_cc: str = "39") -> str: """Return the number as '+<8..15 digits>' (E.164 style); see Chapter 14.""" s = "".join(ch for ch in str(text).strip() if ch not in _SEPARATORS) if s.startswith("+"): body = s[1:] elif s.startswith("00"): body = s[2:] else: body = default_cc + s if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+", body): raise ValueError(f"invalid characters in phone number: {text!r}") if not 8 <= len(body) <= 15: raise ValueError(f"a phone number needs 8-15 digits including the country code: {text!r}") return "+" + body _EMAIL = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$") # deliberately simple @dataclass(frozen=True) class Contact: """One phone-book entry. Instances are always valid (class invariant). Identity (for duplicates): name, surname (case-insensitive) and phone. Sort order: surname, name, phone (case-insensitive). """ name: str surname: str phone: str email: str = "" def __post_init__(self): # frozen dataclass: use object.__setattr__ to store the normalised values name, surname, email = self.name.strip(), self.surname.strip(), self.email.strip() if not name: raise ValueError("the first name must not be empty") if email and not _EMAIL.match(email): raise ValueError(f"invalid e-mail address: {email!r}") object.__setattr__(self, "name", name) object.__setattr__(self, "surname", surname) object.__setattr__(self, "email", email) object.__setattr__(self, "phone", normalize_phone(self.phone)) @property def identity(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]: return (self.name.casefold(), self.surname.casefold(), self.phone) @property def sort_key(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]: return (self.surname.casefold(), self.name.casefold(), self.phone) def __str__(self) -> str: full = f"{self.name} {self.surname}".strip() extra = f" <{self.email}>" if self.email else "" return f"{full:<28} {self.phone}{extra}" def to_dict(self) -> dict: return asdict(self) @classmethod def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "Contact": return cls(name=d["name"], surname=d.get("surname", ""), phone=d["phone"], email=d.get("email", "")) c = Contact(" Ada ", "Lovelace", "+44 20 7946 0000", "ada@example.org") print(Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "06 1234 5678")) # Italian landline: +39 added, leading 0 kept print(c, "|", c.identity) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Mario Rossi +390612345678 Ada Lovelace +442079460000 | ('ada', 'lovelace', '+442079460000') ``` ::: ::: ### `book`: the collection and its rules {.deep} ::: {#6a1a9c68 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} """book — the PhoneBook: a collection of unique contacts. No input/print here.""" from typing import Iterator class PhoneBookError(Exception): """Base class of phone-book errors.""" class DuplicateContactError(PhoneBookError): pass class ContactNotFoundError(PhoneBookError, LookupError): pass class PhoneBook: """Unique contacts, stored in a dict keyed by identity. Invariant: no two stored contacts have the same identity. Costs (n contacts): add/remove/contains O(1) expected; listing O(n log n); search O(n). """ def __init__(self, contacts: list[Contact] | None = None): self._by_id: dict[tuple, Contact] = {} for c in contacts or []: self.add(c) def add(self, c: Contact) -> None: if c.identity in self._by_id: raise DuplicateContactError(f"{c.name} {c.surname} ({c.phone}) is already in the phone book") self._by_id[c.identity] = c def remove(self, c: Contact) -> None: try: del self._by_id[c.identity] except KeyError: raise ContactNotFoundError(str(c)) from None def replace(self, old: Contact, new: Contact) -> None: """Edit: replace old with new, keeping the no-duplicates invariant.""" if old.identity not in self._by_id: raise ContactNotFoundError(str(old)) if new.identity != old.identity and new.identity in self._by_id: raise DuplicateContactError(f"{new.name} {new.surname} ({new.phone}) already exists") del self._by_id[old.identity] self._by_id[new.identity] = new def search(self, text: str) -> list[Contact]: """Contacts whose first or last name contains text (case-insensitive), sorted.""" t = text.strip().casefold() return [c for c in self if t in c.name.casefold() or t in c.surname.casefold()] def search_phone(self, text: str) -> list[Contact]: target = normalize_phone(text) return [c for c in self if c.phone == target] def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Contact]: return iter(sorted(self._by_id.values(), key=lambda c: c.sort_key)) def __len__(self) -> int: return len(self._by_id) def __contains__(self, c: object) -> bool: return isinstance(c, Contact) and c.identity in self._by_id ``` ::: ### `storage`: reliable JSON persistence {.deep} ::: {#09a7ec60 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} """storage — the only module that knows the file format (information hiding).""" import json, os, tempfile from pathlib import Path class CorruptedFileError(PhoneBookError): pass class JsonStorage: def __init__(self, path: str | Path): self.path = Path(path) def load(self) -> tuple[list[Contact], list[str]]: """Return (contacts, warnings). Missing or empty file -> empty phone book.""" try: text = self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") except FileNotFoundError: # EAFP: no race window return [], [f"{self.path.name} not found: starting with an empty phone book"] if not text.strip(): return [], [f"{self.path.name} is empty: starting with an empty phone book"] try: records = json.loads(text) except json.JSONDecodeError as err: raise CorruptedFileError(f"{self.path.name} is not valid JSON") from err contacts, warnings = [], [] for i, rec in enumerate(records if isinstance(records, list) else []): try: contacts.append(Contact.from_dict(rec)) except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as err: # skip bad records, keep the rest warnings.append(f"record {i} skipped: {err}") return contacts, warnings def save(self, contacts) -> None: """Atomic write: temporary file in the same folder, then os.replace.""" self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self.path.parent, prefix=self.path.name, suffix=".tmp") try: with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump([c.to_dict() for c in contacts], f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) f.flush() os.fsync(f.fileno()) os.replace(tmp, self.path) except BaseException: os.unlink(tmp) raise ``` ::: ### `cli`: the console user interface {.deep} ::: {#2ec2eb9e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} """cli — all interaction with the user lives here.""" class ConsoleUI: MENU = [("List all contacts", "list_all"), ("Add a contact", "add"), ("Search by name", "search"), ("Search by phone number", "search_by_phone"), ("Edit a contact", "edit"), ("Delete a contact", "delete"), ("Save and exit", None)] def __init__(self, book: PhoneBook, storage: JsonStorage, input_fn=input, print_fn=print): self.book, self.storage = book, storage self.input, self.print = input_fn, print_fn # injected: testable without a keyboard # ---- validated readers ------------------------------------------------- def ask_text(self, prompt: str, required: bool = True, default: str = "") -> str: while True: text = self.input(prompt).strip() if text or not required: return text or default self.print(" This field cannot be empty.") def ask_choice(self, prompt: str, n: int) -> int: while True: text = self.input(prompt).strip() if text.isdigit() and 1 <= int(text) <= n: return int(text) self.print(f" Please type a number between 1 and {n}.") def ask_yes_no(self, prompt: str) -> bool: while True: text = self.input(prompt + " [y/n] ").strip().casefold() if text in ("y", "yes", "s", "si", "sì"): return True if text in ("n", "no"): return False self.print(" Please answer y or n.") def ask_contact(self, current: Contact | None = None) -> Contact: """Read a valid contact; with `current`, an empty answer keeps the old value.""" while True: hint = (lambda v: f" [{v}]") if current else (lambda v: "") name = self.ask_text(f"First name{hint(current.name if current else '')}: ", required=current is None, default=current.name if current else "") surname = self.ask_text(f"Last name{hint(current.surname if current else '')}: ", required=False, default=current.surname if current else "") phone = self.ask_text(f"Phone{hint(current.phone if current else '')}: ", required=current is None, default=current.phone if current else "") email = self.ask_text(f"E-mail (optional){hint(current.email if current else '')}: ", required=False, default=current.email if current else "") try: return Contact(name, surname, phone, email) except ValueError as err: # the model validates; the UI explains self.print(f" Invalid contact: {err}. Please try again.") def pick(self, candidates: list[Contact]) -> Contact | None: if not candidates: self.print(" No matching contact.") return None for i, c in enumerate(candidates, start=1): self.print(f" {i}) {c}") return candidates[self.ask_choice("Which one? ", len(candidates)) - 1] # ---- features ---------------------------------------------------------- def list_all(self): if len(self.book) == 0: self.print(" The phone book is empty.") for c in self.book: self.print(f" {c}") def add(self): try: self.book.add(self.ask_contact()) self.print(" Contact added.") except DuplicateContactError as err: self.print(f" Not added: {err}.") def search(self): results = self.book.search(self.ask_text("Text to search in first/last name: ")) self.print(f" {len(results)} result(s).") for c in results: self.print(f" {c}") def search_by_phone(self): try: results = self.book.search_phone(self.ask_text("Phone number: ")) except ValueError as err: self.print(f" {err}") return for c in results or []: self.print(f" {c}") if not results: self.print(" No contact with this number.") def edit(self): old = self.pick(self.book.search(self.ask_text("Who do you want to edit? "))) if old is None: return self.print(" Press Enter to keep the current value.") new = self.ask_contact(current=old) try: self.book.replace(old, new) self.print(" Contact updated.") except DuplicateContactError as err: self.print(f" Not updated: {err}.") def delete(self): victim = self.pick(self.book.search(self.ask_text("Who do you want to delete? "))) if victim and self.ask_yes_no(f" Delete {victim.name} {victim.surname}?"): self.book.remove(victim) self.print(" Contact deleted.") # ---- main loop ----------------------------------------------------------- def run(self): self.print(f"Phone book: {len(self.book)} contact(s) loaded.") try: while True: self.print("\nMENU") for i, (label, _) in enumerate(self.MENU, start=1): self.print(f" {i}) {label}") label, action = self.MENU[self.ask_choice("Choose an option: ", len(self.MENU)) - 1] if action is None: break getattr(self, action)() except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError): self.print("\nInterrupted.") finally: # always save on the way out self.storage.save(self.book) self.print(f"Saved {len(self.book)} contact(s) to {self.storage.path.name}. Bye!") def main(path: str = "phonebook.json") -> None: storage = JsonStorage(path) try: contacts, warnings = storage.load() except CorruptedFileError as err: print(f"Error: {err}. The file was left untouched; fix or rename it and restart.") return for w in warnings: print("Note:", w) ConsoleUI(PhoneBook(contacts), storage).run() ``` ::: ### A demonstration of use In Colab or a terminal you would simply call `main()`. To make the demonstration reproducible in this book we **inject** a scripted sequence of answers instead of the keyboard (@sec-try) — including several deliberate mistakes — and print the session transcript. ::: {#4edc23df .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import tempfile from pathlib import Path workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) book_file = workdir / "phonebook.json" def scripted(answers): it = iter(answers) def fake_input(prompt=""): answer = next(it) # raises StopIteration -> we convert to EOFError below print(f"{prompt}{answer}") return answer def safe_input(prompt=""): try: return fake_input(prompt) except StopIteration: raise EOFError return safe_input session_1 = [ "9", "abc", "2", # invalid menu choices, then "Add" "Ada", "Lovelace", "+44 20 7946 0000", "ada@example.org", "2", "Grace", "Hopper", "+1 202 555 0100", "", # add, no e-mail "2", "Alan", "Turing", "12ab", "", # invalid phone -> asked again "Alan", "Turing", "+44 161 496 0000", "", "2", "ada", "LOVELACE", "0044 20 7946 0000", "", # same as Ada (case, 00 prefix) -> refused "1", # list "7", # save and exit ] contacts, notes = JsonStorage(book_file).load() # first start: file missing print("Notes:", notes) ConsoleUI(PhoneBook(contacts), JsonStorage(book_file), input_fn=scripted(session_1)).run() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Notes: ['phonebook.json not found: starting with an empty phone book'] Phone book: 0 contact(s) loaded. In a real project they would live in `tests/test_phonebook.py` and run with `pytest`. ::: {#d939a704 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} def expect(exc, fn, *args): try: fn(*args) except exc: return True return False tests = {} # Contact validation tests["phone keeps leading zero"] = Contact("A", "B", "06 1234 5678").phone == "+390612345678" tests["invalid phone rejected"] = expect(ValueError, Contact, "A", "B", "12ab") tests["empty name rejected"] = expect(ValueError, Contact, " ", "B", "3331234567") # PhoneBook invariant b = PhoneBook([Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3331112222")]) tests["duplicate refused (case-insensitive)"] = expect(DuplicateContactError, b.add, Contact("mario", "ROSSI", "+39 333 111 2222")) b.add(Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3339998888")) tests["homonym with other number allowed"] = len(b) == 2 tests["edit into duplicate refused"] = expect(DuplicateContactError, b.replace, Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3339998888"), Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3331112222")) tests["sorted listing"] = [c.surname for c in PhoneBook([Contact("Z", "Zeta", "3330000001"), Contact("A", "Alfa", "3330000002")])] == ["Alfa", "Zeta"] # Storage tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) tests["missing file -> empty book"] = JsonStorage(tmp / "none.json").load()[0] == [] (tmp / "empty.json").write_text("", encoding="utf-8") tests["empty file -> empty book"] = JsonStorage(tmp / "empty.json").load()[0] == [] (tmp / "bad.json").write_text("[{", encoding="utf-8") tests["corrupted file -> clear error"] = expect(CorruptedFileError, JsonStorage(tmp / "bad.json").load) s = JsonStorage(tmp / "round.json"); s.save(b) tests["save/load round trip"] = set(c.identity for c in s.load()[0]) == set(c.identity for c in b) (tmp / "mixed.json").write_text('[{"name": "Ok", "phone": "3331234567"}, {"name": "Bad", "phone": "x"}]', encoding="utf-8") loaded, warns = JsonStorage(tmp / "mixed.json").load() tests["bad records skipped, good kept"] = len(loaded) == 1 and len(warns) == 1 for name, ok in tests.items(): print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}") print(f"{sum(tests.values())}/{len(tests)} tests passed") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` PASS phone keeps leading zero PASS invalid phone rejected PASS empty name rejected PASS duplicate refused (case-insensitive) PASS homonym with other number allowed PASS edit into duplicate refused PASS sorted listing PASS missing file -> empty book PASS empty file -> empty book PASS corrupted file -> clear error PASS save/load round trip PASS bad records skipped, good kept 12/12 tests passed ``` ::: ::: ### How the reference implementation meets the requirements | Requirement | Where | |---|---| | R1, R5, R10 interactive menu, confirmations, clean exit that saves | `ConsoleUI.run`, `MENU`, `finally: save` | | R2, R3 OOP, separated responsibilities, UI outside the domain | `Contact`, `PhoneBook`, `JsonStorage`, `ConsoleUI` | | R4 motivated data structure | `PhoneBook._by_id` + @tbl-project-structures | | R6 add, list, edit, delete, search | `ConsoleUI.add/list_all/edit/delete/search/search_by_phone` | | R7, R8 JSON persistence; the scripted sessions above | ## Extensions {#sec-project-extensions} 1. **Package and command line.** Split the four blocks into the package layout of @sec-real-package and add an `argparse` entry point (`phonebook --file book.json --search Rossi`, @sec-argv). 2. **Faster search.** Keep a sorted list of `sort_key`s and use binary search (`bisect`, @sec-binary-search) for prefix search by surname in $O(\log n + m)$ for $m$ results. Prove the bound. 3. **Import/export CSV** (@sec-csv) so the phone book can be opened in a spreadsheet, with correct quoting of names containing commas. 4. **Undo.** Keep a stack of inverse operations (add ↔ remove, replace ↔ replace back) and add an *undo* menu entry. 5. **Fuzzy search.** Match names with typos using `difflib.get_close_matches` (standard library). 6. **SQLite backend.** Implement a `SqliteStorage` with the same interface as `JsonStorage` (an abstract base class `Storage`, @sec-inheritance) and switch backends without touching the UI — the payoff of information hiding. 7. **AI-assisted review.** Give an assistant the requirements of @sec-project-brief and your code as a structured prompt (@sec-structured-prompting) and ask for a review and for additional edge-case tests; verify each suggestion before accepting it. ## Further reading {.unnumbered} - The companion notebook: [`Phone_Book_Python_OOP.ipynb`](https://github.com/matteo-zirilli/ai-projects/blob/main/Phone_Book_Python_OOP.ipynb) (English) and its Italian original in the `it/` folder of [`ai-projects`](https://github.com/matteo-zirilli/ai-projects). - @martin2003 — the SOLID principles applied in the design. - @parnas1972 — information hiding: why `JsonStorage` is the only component that knows the file format. - @ramalho2022 — idiomatic data classes and special methods. - @itue164 — the international numbering plan behind `normalize_phone`.
